title: Host capability data (D5b)
description: The verb->mechanism map the host-neutral instruction core defers to. Every field is required except shim_max_lines: a defaulted capability is exactly the silent guess this schema exists to remove, and there is no 'omit it and inherit'. Consumed by multi_llm.py, install-host, hosts/render_capabilities.py and the tests; never by an agent.

provenance_value.description: verified = a recorded live smoke observed it; documented = host docs only; unknown = the shipping default. A documented-only value never selects the non-conservative path.

env_name.description: A literal environment variable name. Wildcards are rejected: a '*' would strip the runner's own credentials along with the host's guard.

override_channel.description: The key/variable the timeout ceiling is raised through, 'none' when the host has no such surface, or 'unknown' until it is confirmed. The installer only ever writes through a non-'none' channel.

template.description: Repo-relative .tmpl path, or null for the one host nobody renders (Claude Code, whose shim path the host fixes for us).

shim_max_lines.description: The ONE optional key. Absent means the ~100 rendered-line budget; present (with a rationale comment) only for a host whose mandatory frontmatter cannot fit inside it. It governs a lint, never a dispatch decision, which is why it is the single field allowed to default.

headless_invocation.description: Optional. The exact headless command line for this host when it differs from the obvious one — a measured fact, not a convention. Present only where getting it wrong fails confusingly rather than loudly (OpenCode's yargs swallows an argument list that starts with a flag and prints its own help instead of running). Absent means the host's documented headless form needs no correction. Governs generated documentation only, never a dispatch decision.

install_paths.description: Per-scope lists in the host's own discovery-precedence order, with $HOME / %USERPROFILE% / $XDG_CONFIG_HOME left as tokens. D7's path matrix is generated from this, never hand-written.

subagents.description: native -> the tool named in native_tool.subagents, executor unused; executor -> --exec-subagents; none -> --exec-subagents, or the run is refused when nested_exec denies the spawn.

ask.description: structured -> the ask tool named in native_tool.ask; free-text -> the numbered-option block, and only under --interactive; none -> the documented --yes default, --interactive rejected with exit 3.

detach.description: native -> the host's own background mechanism; python -> --detach available, foreground still legal; required -> --detach on every fan-out mode.

native_tool.description: The host's own tool name, per verb, wherever that verb resolves to a native mechanism. THE ONLY PLACE a host tool name is allowed to exist anywhere in this skill (outside a shim, which bakes these strings in). Modelled per verb rather than as one string because the three verbs resolve to three different tools on a host like Claude Code.

default_subagent_runner.description: A provider:model spec that must appear in this entry's own runners map.

subagent_tiers.description: The native-host tier->model map (D2e): present when subagents == native, explicit null when that host's native tool takes no model parameter, and forbidden outright otherwise since an executor host reads its tiers from providers.yaml.

nested_exec.description: Whether a third-party agent CLI can actually be exec'd from inside this host's shell with network and auth intact (D3c).

env_guards.description: The HOST-INJECTED variables the executor strips from every dispatched runner's environment. Empty lists are legal and mean 'audited, found nothing'; the field is required precisely so an unaudited host cannot look identical to a clean one — its provenance stays unknown until the diff has run. The runner-side half of the strip list lives in each adapter's get_remove_env(), because it travels with the binary rather than with the host.

max_concurrent_subagents.description: The host-side ceiling in D3i's three-way minimum.

timeout_ceiling_s.description: Seconds a single shell command may run; 0 means no documented cap.

provenance.description: One key per field above (shim_max_lines excepted, being optional). Missing keys fail the completeness test.
